correctness.rationale: At any \(N\geq3\) the regenerative stationary age has density S(t)^N/Z and coordinates are independent killed Brownian variables conditioned on age. The exact Gaussian image tail difference, scaling t=R^2s/(4D), a sharp comparison bound and an integrable s^{-N/2} exp(-B/(2s)) majorant establish the complete joint constant. Substituting u=1/s identifies the Gamma posterior. Positive support is bounded by L, yielding the iff moment cutoff. Conditional mean integration gives positive finite cross-covariance only for \(N\geq5\). A standalone checker passed 60 finite quadrature diagnostics; it is not the infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The complete \(N>2\) stationary law does not by itself state which moments are physically finite or whether arbitrarily far-left events are asymptotically shared. The fixed-population extreme asymptotic identifies a natural universal k-particle contagion coefficient, a Gamma time scale conditional on rare observations, and sharp mean/variance boundaries at populations 4 and 5; these differ substantively from the source large-N typical Gaussian profile and from Poisson-reset exponential tails. This has direct use for rare common-stress and threshold-triggered reliability observables.
